text: The Mayor of Kathmandu is the head of the municipal executive of Kathmandu Metropolitan City, elected for a five-year term with a limit of two consecutive terms. The position was first established in 1932 during the Rana regime. Kathmandu was initially declared a municipality in 1932 through the Kathmandu Municipality Sabal Act, founded as a waste management department, and Singh Shamsher Jung Bahadur Rana was appointed as the first 'Mayor Man' by the government of Chandra Shumsher. In 1947, the first municipal elections were held, with Gehendra Shumsher Thapa appointed as chairman by the Rana regime and Shankar Dev Pant elected as his deputy. Following the fall of the Rana regime in 1953, Janak Man Shrestha became the first elected mayor through an indirect election by the council. After King Mahendra's coup in 1960, the mayor position was abolished, and the Pradhan Panch (Council Head) became the elected head. In 1995, mayor Prem Lal Singh declared Kathmandu a metropolitan city, and Keshav Sthapit was elected as its first mayor in 1997. The position has been held by fifteen individuals in a permanent capacity since its creation. The city is overseen by the Kathmandu Metropolitan City Municipal Assembly, and the mayor is supported by the Municipal Executive, composed of ward chairs from all 32 wards. Local government authority in Nepal is defined under Schedule 8 of the Constitution of Nepal, and the mayor's powers are derived from the Local Government Operation Act, 2017. The mayor's main functions include serving as a member of the Kathmandu District Assembly, an ex-officio member of the Pashupati Area Development Trust, the Boudhanath Area Development Committee, the senate of the National Academy of Medical Sciences, and as chairman of the Valley Municipal Forum. The current mayor is Sunita Dangol, who has been serving since January 18, 2025, and was elected as deputy mayor in the 2022 election, taking office on May 30, 2022.
